       VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION: "high"
       VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND: "trtllm"
     hardware_overrides:
+      # B200 AgentX lane (InferenceX #4382): TP4 on four of the node's eight
+      # GPUs. Per-concurrency --max-num-seqs, active-sequence caps and CUDA
+      # graph sizes are in the guide.
+      b200:
+        docker_image: "vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-af7f9488c2210d67e1033ecdc845b087ee7fe92b"
+        extra_args:
+          - "--enable-prefix-caching"
+          - "--max-num-batched-tokens"
+          - "16384"
+          - "--gpu-memory-utilization"
+          - "0.95"
+          - "--disable-flashinfer-autotune"
+          - "--stream-interval"
+          - "20"
       # GB200 AgentX lane (InferenceX #4281, run 39150937290): one tray per TP4

@@ -777,6 +797,72 @@ guide: |
   --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
   ```
 
+  ## B200: InferenceX AgentX aggregated (vLLM)
+
+  The B200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp` and `minimaxm3-fp4-b200-vllm-agentic-mtp-c10`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4382](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4382)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft as one aggregated vLLM worker on a single 8-GPU B200 node. Most points run TP4; the concurrency-10 arm also has a TP8 point. The two keys use different images: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-af7f9488c2210d67e1033ecdc845b087ee7fe92b@sha256:8e2ffbb9f866de678b22e7446903b1ee5a5766c51a948013277477c462a68a77` for the first and `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-ac7509e2b1db40fec2f03dde1ed4e9dfdc2338c9@sha256:98adb2311118263a453ec0acd5d4b72bda3db26cecc0fe8ffc94b9ab03c951f9` for the second.
+
+  In the command builder, pick **B200** and the **NVFP4** variant (the builder keeps the current variant when you switch hardware, so select NVFP4 explicitly), turn on **Spec Decoding → GQA** and **Text-only**, and use **Single-node TP**. On an 8-GPU B200 node the builder sizes TP to 8, so change `--tensor-parallel-size` to `4` for the TP4 points. That renders the flags and environment below as a `vllm serve` command; the per-point settings in the tables stay in this guide. The B200 **Verified** badge is recipe-wide; this profile covers the NVFP4 variant only, and the GQA draft override also applies to the other variants on B200, which were not qualified.
+
+  For the host-KV-offload points, don't use the **KV Offload → Simple** pill as is: replace its `--kv-transfer-config` with the qualified one below and set `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`.
+
+  ### `-vllm-agentic-mtp` (three-token draft, `nightly-af7f9488`)
+
+  Every point uses the GQA draft with FlashInfer draft attention and local argmax reduction, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm`.
+
+  | Clients | TP | `--max-num-seqs` | Host KV offload | `--max-cudagraph-capture-size` |
+  |---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
+  | 15 | 4 | 30 | none | 120 |
+  | 30 | 4 | 60 | SimpleCPUOffload | 4096 (explicit list below) |
+  | 32 | 4 | 64 | SimpleCPUOffload | 256 |
+  | 38 | 4 | 76 | SimpleCPUOffload | 4096 (explicit list below) |
+
+  The concurrency-30 and -38 points also set `"minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend":"cutlass"` in `--attention-config` (the builder's NVFP4 default) and an explicit `--cudagraph-capture-sizes`:
+
+  - 30: `1,2,4,8`, every 8 from `16` to `232`, then `240,256,320,384,448,512,640,768,896,1024,1280,1536,1792,2048,2560,3072,3584,4096`
+  - 38: `1,2,4,8`, every 8 from `16` to `248`, then `256,272,288,304,320,384,448,512,640,768,896,1024,1280,1536,1792,2048,2560,3072,3584,4096`
+
+  The other points omit `minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend`, so the pinned image's default applies.
+
+  ### `-vllm-agentic-mtp-c10` (active-sequence caps, `nightly-ac7509e2`)
+
+  These arms cap the number of sequences the scheduler keeps active with `--max-num-active-seqs`, well below the client count, and set `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=mnnvl`. They use the GQA draft with FlashInfer draft attention but without local argmax reduction, and leave `--max-num-seqs` at its default.
+
+  | Clients | TP | `--max-num-active-seqs` | Draft tokens | Host KV offload | `--gpu-memory-utilization` |
+  |---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
+  | 10 | 4 | 1 | 5 | none | 0.925 |
+  | 10 | 8 | 1 | 5 | none | 0.9 (FlashInfer autotune on) |
+  | 20 | 4 | 4 | 3 | SimpleCPUOffload | 0.9 |
+  | 20 | 4 | 3 | 3 | SimpleCPUOffload | 0.9 |
+  | 32 | 4 | 6 | 3 | SimpleCPUOffload | 0.925 |
+  | 32 | 4 | 16 | 3 | SimpleCPUOffload | 0.925 |
+
+  The draft is `{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA","num_speculative_tokens":<K>,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER"}`. Every point sets `--max-cudagraph-capture-size` to the last entry of its `--cudagraph-capture-sizes`: `1,2,4,8`, every 4 from `12` to `256`, every 16 from `272` to `512`, then `640,768,1024,1536,2048,3072,4096` (max `4096`). The concurrency-20 points append `6144,8192` (max `8192`).
+
+  ### Host KV offload
+
+  ```bash
+  export VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1
+  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":1073000000000,"lazy_offload":true}}'
+  ```
+
+  That is 1,073 GB of pinned host memory for KV blocks across the node.
+
+  ### Command
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm \
+  vllm serve nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code \
+    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","use_trtllm_attention":true,"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}' \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs <S> --max-cudagraph-capture-size <N> \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --disable-flashinfer-autotune --stream-interval 20 --language-model-only \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking_mode":"enabled"}'
+  ```
+
+  The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler, as in the command above.
+
   ## GB200: InferenceX AgentX aggregated (Dynamo + vLLM)
 
   The GB200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-agg-mtp`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4281](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4281)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three speculative tokens) as one aggregated vLLM worker behind the Dynamo frontend's KV-aware router. TP4 runs on one 4-GPU GB200 tray; TP8 spans two trays. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-5555a2d8f7116b2b4877f66516f4128176cf722a@sha256:8896fd7b29fc4ee7ce839f146cb4757984c476ec79d0234ffa8c995dee6e339a`, Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016` (`pip install ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261016`).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.mm.lora import set_active_mm_loras
+
+
+class _FakeModel:
+    """Records calls to get_mm_lora_token_counts so the test can assert it
+    is never invoked for the "prompt_embeds" passthrough modality."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.calls: list[str] = []
+
+    def get_mm_lora_token_counts(self, *, modality, mm_kwargs, num_mm_embeds):
+        del mm_kwargs
+        self.calls.append(modality)
+        return num_mm_embeds, num_mm_embeds
+
+    def get_mm_mapping(self):
+        return SimpleNamespace(connector=None)
+
+
+class _FakeLoRAManager:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.set_active_adapters_calls: list[tuple] = []
+
+    def supports_tower_connector_lora(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    def set_active_adapters(self, requests, mapping) -> None:
+        self.set_active_adapters_calls.append((requests, mapping))
+
+
+def _mm_feature(modality: str, num_embeds: int):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        modality=modality,
+        data=None,
+        mm_position=SimpleNamespace(get_num_embeds=lambda: num_embeds),
+    )
+
+
+def test_set_active_mm_loras_skips_prompt_embeds_passthrough():
+    """`prompt_embeds` is a passthrough modality: the tensor is already in
+    the model's embedding space, no encoder runs, and there is nothing to
+    apply tower/connector LoRA to. set_active_mm_loras must skip it instead
+    of forwarding it to the model's get_mm_lora_token_counts (which doesn't
+    know about it and would raise "Unsupported modality")."""
+    req_id = "req-0"
+    model = _FakeModel()
+    lora_manager = _FakeLoRAManager()
+    encoder_cache = SimpleNamespace(
+        mm_features={
+            req_id: [
+                _mm_feature("prompt_embeds", num_embeds=32),
+                _mm_feature("image", num_embeds=4),
+            ]
+        }
+    )
+    lora_state = SimpleNamespace(
+        lora_ids=np.array([7], dtype=np.int32),
+        lora_requests={req_id: object()},
+    )
+
+    set_active_mm_loras(
+        model=model,
+        lora_manager=lora_manager,
+        encoder_cache=encoder_cache,
+        req_id_to_index={req_id: 0},
+        lora_state=lora_state,
+        scheduled_encoder_inputs={req_id: [0, 1]},
+    )
+
+    # Only the real "image" item should ever reach the model.
+    assert model.calls == ["image"]
+    assert len(lora_manager.set_active_adapters_calls) == 1
+    _, mapping = lora_manager.set_active_adapters_calls[0]
+    assert mapping.index_mapping == (7, 7, 7, 7)

@@ -40,7 +40,14 @@ def set_active_mm_loras(
 
         lora_id = int(lora_state.lora_ids[req_idx])
         mm_features = encoder_cache.mm_features[req_id]
-        mm_items.extend((lora_id, mm_features[i]) for i in encoder_input_ids)
+        # "prompt_embeds" is a passthrough modality: the tensor is already in
+        # the model's embedding space, so no encoder runs and there is no
+        # tower or connector output to apply LoRA to.
+        mm_items.extend(
+            (lora_id, mm_features[i])
+            for i in encoder_input_ids
+            if mm_features[i].modality != "prompt_embeds"
+        )
 
         if lora_id > 0:
             lora_request = lora_state.lora_requests.get(req_id)

+  prefill_dbo_sp:
+    label: "DBO / SP prefill"
+    description: "AMD MI355X single node: faster long prefill steps. DBO (dual-batch overlap) splits a prefill step into two microbatches and runs one microbatch's all-reduce under the other's compute; decode steps are never split. SP (sequence-parallel prefill) keeps the residual stream sharded by tokens on steps of 4096+ tokens, so each layer's two all-reduces become an all-to-all and a reduce-scatter; it keeps a full o_proj copy per GPU (about 3.1 GB less KV cache)."
+    # Tested on the single-node TP4 engine only (not on a PD prefill node).
+    strategies: [single_node_tp]
+    default_mode: sp_dbo
+    # SP + DBO and SP were run on the default checkpoint only (MXFP8 MoE).
+    modes:
+      sp_dbo:
+        variants: [default]
+        label: "SP + DBO"
+        description: "SP prefill, and DBO on prefill steps of 16384+ tokens: each microbatch then has 8192+ tokens and stays on the SP path."
+        # DBO needs the V2 model runner: without it, --enable-dbo selects the
+        # V1 runner, which refuses the DSpark draft.
+        args:
+          - "--enable-dbo"
+          - "--dbo-prefill-token-threshold"
+          - "16384"

+  ### DBO and SP prefill (TP4, AMD MI355X)
+
+  Two opt-in switches make long prefill steps faster on the single-node MI355X
+  engine (the **DBO / SP prefill** feature in the command builder):
+
+  - **DBO** (dual-batch overlap): `--enable-dbo` splits a prefill step into two
+    microbatches and runs one microbatch's all-reduce under the other's compute.
+    `--dbo-decode-token-threshold 32768` keeps decode steps whole. DBO needs
+    `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`: without it, `--enable-dbo` selects the V1
+    runner, which refuses the DSpark draft.
+  - **SP** (sequence-parallel prefill): `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_SP_PREFILL=1`
+    keeps the residual stream sharded by tokens on steps of 4096+ tokens, so
+    each layer's two all-reduces become an all-to-all and a reduce-scatter. It
+    keeps a full `o_proj` copy per GPU, about 3.1 GB less KV cache.
+  - **SP + DBO**: set both, with `--dbo-prefill-token-threshold 16384`, so each
+    DBO microbatch has 8192+ tokens and stays on the SP path.
+
+  On the MXFP8 MoE, one 32K-token prefill takes 1035 ms plain, 655 ms with DBO
+  and 484 ms with SP + DBO. The server log confirms SP with
+  `MiniMax-M3 sequence-parallel prefill (from 4096 tokens, DBO microbatches from 8192): on`.

+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("image_counts", [(1, 3), (3, 1)])
+def test_deepseek_vl2_encoder_cache_cropping(
+    vllm_runner: type[VllmRunner], image_counts: tuple[int, int]
+):
+    images = [Image.new("RGB", (768, 768), color) for color in ("red", "green", "blue")]
+    with vllm_runner(
+        "deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny",
+        hf_overrides={"architectures": ["DeepseekVLV2ForCausalLM"]},
+        max_model_len=4096,
+        max_num_seqs=1,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 3},
+    ) as runner:
+        for count in image_counts:
+            prompt = "<|User|>: " + "<image>\n" * count + "Describe.\n\n<|Assistant|>:"
+            outputs = runner.llm.generate(
+                {"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": images[:count]}},
+                SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1),
+            )
+            output = outputs[0].outputs[0]
+            # A cache collision makes the scheduler reject the second request
+            # with finish_reason="error" due to mismatched embedding counts.
+            assert output.finish_reason == "length"
+            assert len(output.token_ids) == 1

+    tokenizer = processor.info.get_tokenizer()
+    images = [

+    results = []

+    hashes = [result["mm_hashes"]["image"][0] for result in results]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import FunctionCall, ToolCall
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
+    ChatCompletionNamedToolChoiceParam,
+    ChatCompletionRequest,
+)
+from vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils.tool_calls_utils import (
+    maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls,
+)
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.parser.abstract_parser import Parser
+from vllm.renderers.chat_utils import make_tool_call_id
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class ChatMessageFields(NamedTuple):
+    reasoning: str | None
+    content: str | None
+    tool_calls: list[ToolCall]
+
+
+def assemble_chat_message_fields(
+    request: ChatCompletionRequest,
+    reasoning: str | None,
+    content: str | None,
+    tool_calls: list[FunctionCall] | None,
+    *,
+    enable_auto_tools: bool,
+    parser_cls: type[Parser] | None,
+) -> ChatMessageFields:
+    """Pick the assistant message fields for one parsed chat choice.
+
+    Shared by `OpenAIServingChat` and batch chat derender so both surface the
+    same `reasoning`, `content` and `tool_calls` for the same parser output.
+
+    Args:
+        request: Supplies `tools`, `tool_choice`, `include_reasoning` and
+            `parallel_tool_calls`.
+        reasoning: Reasoning from `Parser.parse`.
+        content: Content from `Parser.parse` or the raw text without a parser.
+        tool_calls: Tool calls from `Parser.parse`.
+        enable_auto_tools: The server's `--enable-auto-tool-choice`.
+        parser_cls: The server's parser class, if any.
+
+    Returns:
+        The fields for the response `ChatMessage`.
+
+    """
+    if not request.include_reasoning:
+        reasoning = None
+
+    tool_choice = request.tool_choice
+    if (
+        type(tool_choice) is ChatCompletionNamedToolChoiceParam
+        or tool_choice == "required"
+    ):
+        return ChatMessageFields(
+            reasoning, content or "", _to_tool_calls(tool_calls, request)
+        )
+
+    auto_tools = (
+        enable_auto_tools
+        and parser_cls is not None
+        and parser_cls.tool_parser_cls is not None
+    )
+    if auto_tools and tool_choice == "auto":
+        if request.tools:
+            return ChatMessageFields(

@@ -0,0 +1,635 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiniCPM-OCR semantics that differ from MiniCPM-V 4.6.
+
+The model code is inherited wholesale, so what needs pinning is the image
+geometry: the `"4x"` patch-grid alignment, and the fact that the image
+placeholder is measured from the `target_sizes` the image processor returned
+rather than recomputed from the image dimensions.
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.models.minicpm_ocr import (
+    _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS,
+    MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor,
+    MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.models.minicpmv4_6 import MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor
+from vllm.multimodal.parse import ImageSize
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup
+
+_PATCH_SIZE = 14
+_SCALE_RESOLUTION = 448
+
+
+def ensure_divide(length: int, divisor: int) -> int:
+    """Copy of `transformers.models.minicpmv4_6...ensure_divide`."""
+    return max(round(length / divisor) * divisor, divisor)
+
+
+class _StubImageProcessor:
+    """Stands in for `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor`.
+
+    `find_best_resize` and `get_sliced_grid`/`get_refine_size` are transcribed
+    from `modular_minicpm_ocr.py` / `image_processing_minicpmv4_6.py` so the
+    geometry under test is the real one, without needing a checkpoint or an
+    installed transformers build that carries the model.
+    """
+
+    downsample_mode = "4x"
+    max_slice_nums = 9
+    scale_resolution = _SCALE_RESOLUTION
+    patch_size = _PATCH_SIZE
+    slice_mode = True
+
+    def find_best_resize(
+        self, image_size, scale_resolution, patch_size, allow_upscale=False
+    ):
+        height, width = image_size
+        if (height * width > scale_resolution * scale_resolution) or allow_upscale:
+            aspect_ratio = width / height
+            height = int(scale_resolution / math.sqrt(aspect_ratio))
+            width = int(height * aspect_ratio)
+        # The OCR delta: one 2x2 merge in "4x" mode, two in "16x".
+        merge_factor = 2 if self.downsample_mode == "4x" else 4
+        best_width = ensure_divide(width, patch_size * merge_factor)
+        best_height = ensure_divide(height, patch_size * merge_factor)
+        return best_height, best_width
+
+    def get_refine_size(
+        self, image_size, grid, scale_resolution, patch_size, allow_upscale=False
+    ):
+        height, width = image_size
+        grid_y, grid_x = grid
+        refine_width = ensure_divide(width, grid_x)
+        refine_height = ensure_divide(height, grid_y)
+        best_height, best_width = self.find_best_resize(
+            (refine_height / grid_y, refine_width / grid_x),
+            scale_resolution,
+            patch_size,
+            allow_upscale=allow_upscale,
+        )
+        return best_height * grid_y, best_width * grid_x
+
+    def get_sliced_grid(self, image_size, max_slice_nums, scale_resolution):
+        original_height, original_width = image_size
+        log_ratio = math.log(original_width / original_height)
+        ratio = original_width * original_height / (scale_resolution**2)
+        multiple = min(math.ceil(ratio), max_slice_nums)
+        if multiple <= 1:
+            return None
+
+        candidate_split_grids_nums = []
+        for i in [multiple - 1, multiple, multiple + 1]:
+            if i == 1 or i > max_slice_nums:
+                continue
+            candidate_split_grids_nums.append(i)
+
+        candidate_grids = []
+        for split_grids_nums in candidate_split_grids_nums:
+            m = 1
+            while m <= split_grids_nums:
+                if split_grids_nums % m == 0:
+                    candidate_grids.append([m, split_grids_nums // m])
+                m += 1
+
+        best_grid = [1, 1]
+        min_error = float("inf")
+        for grid in candidate_grids:
+            error = abs(log_ratio - math.log(grid[0] / grid[1]))
+            if error < min_error:
+                best_grid = grid
+                min_error = error
+        return best_grid
+
+
+class _StubTokenizer:
+    image_token = "<|image_pad|>"
+    image_start_token = "<image>"
+    image_end_token = "</image>"
+    slice_start_token = "<slice>"
+    slice_end_token = "</slice>"
+    image_id_start_token = "<image_id>"
+    image_id_end_token = "</image_id>"
+
+
+def _make_info(**processor_attrs) -> MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo:
+    info = MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo.__new__(MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+    image_processor = _StubImageProcessor()
+    for key, value in processor_attrs.items():
+        setattr(image_processor, key, value)
+
+    info.get_image_processor = lambda **kwargs: image_processor  # type: ignore[method-assign]
+    info.get_tokenizer = lambda: _StubTokenizer()  # type: ignore[method-assign,return-value]
+    return info
+
+
+def _make_processor(info: MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo):
+    processor = MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor.__new__(MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor)
+    processor.info = info
+    return processor
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Geometry: "4x" aligns to patch_size * 2, not patch_size * 4
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_4x_mode_aligns_the_patch_grid_to_two_patches():
+    """The resize grid follows the number of 2x2 merges, not just the divisor.
+
+    `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize` aligns to `patch_size * 2` in
+    `"4x"` mode, so a 4.6-style alignment would round the grid to a different
+    size and the vision tower and the placeholder would disagree.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=300, height=200)
+
+    grids_4x, source_4x, patch_4x = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="4x"
+    )
+    grids_16x, source_16x, patch_16x = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="16x"
+    )
+
+    # Not sliced: 300*200 < 448^2.
+    assert grids_4x == [0, 0]
+    assert grids_16x == [0, 0]
+    assert patch_4x == 0 and patch_16x == 0
+
+    # Upscaled to ~448 on the long side, then aligned: "4x" rounds to 28px and
+    # "16x" to 56px, which lands on a different grid for the same image.
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor("4x").find_best_resize(
+        (200, 300), _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+    ) == (364, 560)
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor("16x").find_best_resize(
+        (200, 300), _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+    ) == (392, 560)
+
+    # 364*560 / (14*14*4) = 260 against 392*560 / (14*14*16) = 70: the ratio is
+    # not a clean 4x precisely because the alignment differs, which is what a
+    # 4.6-style `find_best_resize` would get wrong.
+    assert source_4x == 260
+    assert source_16x == 70
+
+
+def test_pinned_processor_does_not_mutate_the_shared_instance():
+    """A per-request mode must not leak into the shared image processor.
+
+    `find_best_resize` reads `downsample_mode` off the instance, and the engine
+    reuses one processor across requests.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    shared = info.get_image_processor()
+    assert shared.downsample_mode == "4x"
+
+    pinned = info._pinned_image_processor("16x")
+    assert pinned is not shared
+    assert pinned.downsample_mode == "16x"
+    assert shared.downsample_mode == "4x"
+
+    # The default mode needs no copy at all.
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor("4x") is shared
+    assert info._pinned_image_processor(None) is shared
+
+
+def test_downsample_mode_defaults_to_the_processor_value():
+    """OCR checkpoints ship `downsample_mode: "4x"`; 4.6's fallback is "16x"."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    assert info._get_downsample_mode() == "4x"
+    assert info._get_downsample_mode("16x") == "16x"
+
+    # The fallback only applies when the processor carries no value at all.
+    bare = _make_info()
+    del type(bare.get_image_processor()).downsample_mode
+    try:
+        assert bare._get_downsample_mode() == "16x"
+    finally:
+        _StubImageProcessor.downsample_mode = "4x"
+
+
+def test_sliced_image_token_counts_match_the_transformers_divisor():
+    """Sliced geometry: source + grid*patch tokens, counted with divisor 4."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+
+    grids, source_tokens, patch_tokens = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="4x"
+    )
+
+    assert grids != [0, 0]
+    processor = info._pinned_image_processor("4x")
+    refine = processor.get_refine_size(
+        (1120, 1680), grids, _SCALE_RESOLUTION, _PATCH_SIZE, allow_upscale=True
+    )
+    expected_patch = (
+        (refine[0] // grids[0])
+        * (refine[1] // grids[1])
+        // (_PATCH_SIZE * _PATCH_SIZE * 4)
+    )
+    assert patch_tokens == expected_patch
+    assert source_tokens > 0
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Placeholder measured from target_sizes
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _placeholder(info, tgt_sizes, image_size, *, image_idx=0, mode="4x"):
+    processor = _make_processor(info)
+    return processor._ocr_image_prompt_text(
+        torch.tensor(tgt_sizes, dtype=torch.long),
+        image_size,
+        image_idx,
+        downsample_mode=mode,
+        max_slice_nums=None,
+    )
+
+
+def test_placeholder_is_counted_from_target_sizes():
+    """Token count mirrors `MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`.
+
+    That method computes `target_sizes.prod(-1) // token_divisor` per patch.
+    Reproducing it here is what keeps the count right under
+    `adaptive_small_image_upsize`, whose resize target is decided from the
+    pixels and so is invisible to a size-only computation.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    # An unsliced image: one row only.
+    text = _placeholder(info, [[8, 8]], ImageSize(width=112, height=112))
+
+    # 8*8 = 64 patches, divisor 4 -> 16 tokens.
+    assert text == ("<image_id>0</image_id><image>" + "<|image_pad|>" * 16 + "</image>")
+
+
+def test_adaptive_upsize_changes_the_count_without_changing_the_image_size():
+    """Two tiers of the same image must yield different placeholders.
+
+    `adaptive_upsize_tier` can send a small image to `scale_resolution` or to
+    `adaptive_upsize_tiny_target_resolution`, and `ImageSize` is identical in
+    both cases. This is exactly the divergence that counting from `image_size`
+    would miss.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=80, height=80)
+
+    native = _placeholder(info, [[4, 4]], image_size)
+    tier2 = _placeholder(info, [[6, 6]], image_size)
+    tier1 = _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]], image_size)
+
+    assert native.count("<|image_pad|>") == 4
+    assert tier2.count("<|image_pad|>") == 9
+    assert tier1.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64
+
+    # And the size-only path cannot tell them apart: it always upscales to
+    # `scale_resolution`, so all three tiers would be counted as 448*448 worth
+    # of tokens regardless of what the processor actually produced.
+    _, size_only_tokens, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+        image_size, downsample_mode="4x"
+    )
+    assert size_only_tokens == 256
+    assert size_only_tokens not in (4, 9, 64)
+
+
+def test_placeholder_emits_the_slice_grid_from_the_geometry():
+    """Slice rows come from `get_sliced_grid`, which is not pixel-dependent."""
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+    grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(image_size, downsample_mode="4x")
+    num_slices = grids[0] * grids[1]
+
+    tgt_sizes = [[16, 16]] + [[8, 8]] * num_slices
+    text = _placeholder(info, tgt_sizes, image_size)
+
+    assert text is not None
+    assert text.count("<slice>") == num_slices
+    assert text.count("\n") == grids[0] - 1
+    # 16*16/4 source tokens + one 8*8/4 block per slice.
+    assert text.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64 + 16 * num_slices
+
+
+def test_placeholder_emits_differing_tiles_one_by_one():
+    """`adaptive_tile_upsize` can leave tiles at different resolutions.
+
+    Each slice then gets its own count instead of row 1 repeated.
+    """
+    info = _make_info()
+    image_size = ImageSize(width=1680, height=1120)
+    grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(image_size, downsample_mode="4x")
+    num_rows, num_cols = grids
+    num_slices = num_rows * num_cols
+
+    tile_sizes = [[8 + (i % 2) * 4, 8 + (i % 2) * 4] for i in range(num_slices)]
+    text = _placeholder(info, [[16, 16]] + tile_sizes, image_size)
+
+    assert text is not None
+    assert text.count("<slice>") == num_slices
+    per_tile = sum(size[0] * size[1] // 4 for size in tile_sizes)
+    assert text.count("<|image_pad|>") == 64 + per_tile
+
+
+def test_video_path_pins_the_upsize_defaults(monkeypatch):
+    """Frames must be counted the same way `_compute_visual_tokens` counts them.
+
+    `_drop_image_upsize_kwargs` only removes request keys; the loaded processor
+    still applies its own defaults per frame, so they are pinned too.
+    """
+    captured = {}
+
+    def fake_process_videos(self, mm_data, mm_kwargs):
+        captured.update(mm_kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor, "process_videos", fake_process_videos
+    )
+    processor = _processor_with_merge({})
+    processor.process_videos(
+        {},
+        {"downsample_mode": "4x", "adaptive_small_image_upsize": True},
+    )
+
+    assert captured["downsample_mode"] == "4x"
+    assert captured["adaptive_small_image_upsize"] is False
+    assert captured["disable_small_image_upsize"] is False
+    assert captured["adaptive_tile_upsize"] is False
+
+
+def test_placeholder_falls_back_when_target_sizes_disagree_with_the_grid():
+    """A mismatch must not silently emit a count we cannot justify.
+

+def _transformers_replace_image_token(
+    target_sizes, grids, num_patches_per_image, image_idx, image_token_divisor
+):
+    """Transcription of `MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`.
+
+    Kept verbatim (minus the tokenizer attribute lookups) so the count under
+    test is compared against the transformers formula itself rather than
+    against a number restated in the assertion. Note the divisor is applied to
+    `target_sizes` directly: that tensor is already in patch units.
+    """
+    cum_patches = np.cumsum(num_patches_per_image)
+    start_idx = cum_patches[image_idx - 1] if image_idx > 0 else 0
+    end_idx = cum_patches[image_idx]
+    img_target_sizes = target_sizes[start_idx:end_idx]
+    num_tokens_per_patch = img_target_sizes.prod(-1) // image_token_divisor
+    num_rows, num_cols = grids[image_idx]
+
+    image_placeholder = (
+        "<image>" + "<|image_pad|>" * int(num_tokens_per_patch[0]) + "</image>"
+    )
+    if num_rows > 0 and num_cols > 0:
+        per_slice = int(num_tokens_per_patch[1]) if len(num_tokens_per_patch) > 1 else 0
+        slice_placeholder = "<slice>" + "<|image_pad|>" * per_slice + "</slice>"
+        slices = [slice_placeholder * num_cols for _ in range(num_rows)]
+        image_placeholder += "\n".join(slices)
+    return image_placeholder

+"""Inference-only MiniCPM-OCR model.
+
+Same vision/LLM stack as MiniCPM-V 4.6. ``MiniCPMOcrForConditionalGeneration``
+is a plain subclass of ``MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration`` in transformers
+too; what differs is the image geometry:
+
+* ``downsample_mode`` defaults to ``"4x"``, and in that mode
+  ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize`` aligns the patch grid to
+  ``patch_size * 2`` instead of ``patch_size * 4``, because ``"4x"`` goes
+  through one 2x2 merge (downsample MLP) rather than two (ViT insert merger as
+  well).
+* An image small enough not to be sliced may be resized to a target picked from
+  its own pixels (``adaptive_small_image_upsize``) or kept at its native
+  resolution (``disable_small_image_upsize``).
+
+The second point is why the image placeholder here is measured from the
+``target_sizes`` the image processor actually returned rather than recomputed
+from the image dimensions: the adaptive tier is decided by an Otsu threshold
+plus connected-component analysis over the pixels, which a size-only
+reimplementation cannot reproduce. This mirrors
+``MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token``, which reads the same tensor.
+"""
+
+import copy
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import replace as dataclass_replace
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+from vllm.multimodal.parse import ImageProcessorItems, ImageSize
+from vllm.multimodal.processing.processor import (
+    PromptUpdateDetails,
+    cached_encode,
+)
+
+from .minicpmv import MiniCPMVDummyInputsBuilder, MiniCPMVImageEmbeddingItems
+from .minicpmv4_6 import (
+    MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration,
+    MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor,
+    MiniCPMV4_6ProcessingInfo,
+    _scoped_mm_kwarg,
+)
+
+# Options declared by `MiniCPMOcrImageProcessorKwargs` on top of the 4.6 set.
+# `MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessorKwargs` deliberately declares none of them: in
+# transformers videos go through `MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessor`, which has no
+# small-image upsize logic at all.
+_OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS = (
+    "disable_small_image_upsize",
+    "adaptive_small_image_upsize",
+    "adaptive_upsize_font_px",
+    "adaptive_upsize_dense_per_kpx",
+    "adaptive_upsize_tiny_pixels",
+    "adaptive_upsize_tiny_target_resolution",
+    "adaptive_tile_upsize",
+)
+
+# Pinned for video frames: `_compute_visual_tokens` counts an unsliced frame as
+# upscaled to `scale_resolution` with uniform tiles, but `process_videos` runs
+# the image processor, whose own defaults are not visible to that count.
+_VIDEO_PINNED_UPSIZE_KWARGS = {
+    "disable_small_image_upsize": False,
+    "adaptive_small_image_upsize": False,
+    "adaptive_tile_upsize": False,
+}
+
+
+class MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo(MiniCPMV4_6ProcessingInfo):
+    def _pinned_image_processor(self, downsample_mode: str | None = None):
+        """Image processor view pinned to the mode resolved for this request.
+
+        ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize`` reads ``downsample_mode``
+        off the instance, so a per-request override only reaches it through the
+        shallow copy that ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.__call__`` makes. Measure
+        the token count on a copy pinned the same way, otherwise the pixels are
+        aligned to one grid and the placeholder is counted on another.
+        """
+        image_processor = self.get_image_processor()
+        resolved = self._get_downsample_mode(downsample_mode)
+        if getattr(image_processor, "downsample_mode", None) == resolved:
+            return image_processor
+
+        pinned = copy.copy(image_processor)
+        pinned.downsample_mode = resolved
+        return pinned
+
+    def get_image_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize:
+        # OCR-only override: source the dummy-input dimension from the image
+        # processor's `scale_resolution` (the slice resize target) rather than the
+        # top-level `config.image_size`. The top-level field is dropped from
+        # `MiniCPMOcrConfig`, and the existing default of 448 was always equal to
+        # `scale_resolution` here. `vision_config.image_size` is the ViT patch grid
+        # (980 for this checkpoint), not the preprocessed image dimension, so it is
+        # not the right value for dummy-input sizing.
+        image_size = self.get_image_processor().scale_resolution
+        max_slice_num = self.get_image_max_slice_num()
+        return ImageSize(width=image_size, height=image_size * max_slice_num)
+
+    def get_video_frame_size_with_most_features(self) -> ImageSize:
+        # See `get_image_size_with_most_features` for why OCR sources from
+        # `scale_resolution` instead of the (now-removed) top-level `config.image_size`.
+        image_size = self.get_image_processor().scale_resolution
+        max_slice_num = self.get_video_max_slice_num()
+        return ImageSize(width=image_size, height=image_size * max_slice_num)
+
+    def _compute_visual_tokens(
+        self,
+        image_size: ImageSize,
+        max_slice_nums: int | None = None,
+        downsample_mode: str | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[list[int], int, int]:
+        """Grid, source tokens and per-slice tokens for one image.
+
+        Same contract as 4.6, re-derived on the pinned processor so that the
+        ``"4x"`` patch-grid alignment is applied.
+
+        The unsliced branch upscales to ``scale_resolution``, which is what
+        ``MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor._preprocess`` does for the default options
+        and what the video path does unconditionally. The remaining
+        ``*_small_image_upsize`` combinations depend on the pixels, so for
+        images the placeholder is taken from ``target_sizes`` instead; see
+        ``MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor._ocr_image_prompt_text``.
+        """
+        image_processor = self._pinned_image_processor(downsample_mode)
+        if max_slice_nums is None:
+            max_slice_nums = image_processor.max_slice_nums
+
+        patch_size = image_processor.patch_size
+        scale_res = image_processor.scale_resolution
+        token_divisor = 4 if image_processor.downsample_mode == "4x" else 16
+        tokens_per_patch = patch_size * patch_size * token_divisor
+
+        # vLLM ImageSize is (width, height); transformers expects (height, width)
+        hf_image_size = (image_size.height, image_size.width)
+
+        grids = image_processor.get_sliced_grid(
+            hf_image_size,
+            max_slice_nums,
+            scale_res,
+        )
+
+        if grids is None:
+            best_size = image_processor.find_best_resize(
+                hf_image_size,
+                scale_res,
+                patch_size,
+                allow_upscale=True,
+            )
+            source_tokens = best_size[0] * best_size[1] // tokens_per_patch
+            return [0, 0], source_tokens, 0
+
+        best_resize = image_processor.find_best_resize(
+            hf_image_size,
+            scale_res,
+            patch_size,
+        )
+        source_tokens = best_resize[0] * best_resize[1] // tokens_per_patch
+
+        refine_size = image_processor.get_refine_size(
+            hf_image_size,
+            grids,
+            scale_res,
+            patch_size,
+            allow_upscale=True,
+        )
+        patch_h = refine_size[0] // grids[0]
+        patch_w = refine_size[1] // grids[1]
+        patch_tokens = patch_h * patch_w // tokens_per_patch
+        return grids, source_tokens, patch_tokens
+
+
+class MiniCPMOcrMultiModalProcessor(MiniCPMV4_6MultiModalProcessor):
+    def _promote_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Resolve the OCR-only upsize options into the flat form.
+
+        ``process_images`` forwards flat keys only (``_flat_processor_kwargs``
+        drops the nested scopes), and 4.6 recovers just ``downsample_mode`` /
+        ``max_slice_nums`` from the merge. Resolve the OCR options the same way
+        so that a server-level ``mm_processor_kwargs`` value, and the nested
+        ``images_kwargs`` form, both reach the image processor instead of being
+        silently dropped.
+        """
+        info = self.info
+        assert isinstance(info, MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+        merged = info._merge_and_resolve_mm_processor_kwargs(mm_kwargs)
+
+        promoted = {}
+        for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS:
+            value = _scoped_mm_kwarg(merged, "image", key)
+            if value is not None:
+                promoted[key] = value
+
+        if not promoted:
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {**mm_kwargs, **promoted}
+
+    def _drop_image_upsize_kwargs(
+        self,
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+        """Remove the image-only upsize options from the video path.
+
+        ``process_videos`` runs the *image* processor per frame, so a flat
+        upsize option would reach frames as well. In transformers frames go
+        through ``MiniCPMOcrVideoProcessor``, which never applies these, and
+        the video placeholder is counted without them.
+        """
+        if not any(key in mm_kwargs for key in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS):
+            return mm_kwargs
+        return {
+            key: value
+            for key, value in mm_kwargs.items()
+            if key not in _OCR_IMAGE_UPSIZE_KWARGS
+        }
+
+    def process_images(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_images(
+            mm_data,
+            self._promote_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+        )
+
+    def process_videos(
+        self,
+        mm_data: Mapping[str, object],
+        mm_kwargs: Mapping[str, object],
+    ):
+        return super().process_videos(
+            mm_data,
+            {
+                **self._drop_image_upsize_kwargs(mm_kwargs),
+                **_VIDEO_PINNED_UPSIZE_KWARGS,
+            },
+        )
+
+    def _ocr_image_prompt_text(
+        self,
+        tgt_sizes: torch.Tensor,
+        image_size: ImageSize,
+        image_idx: int,

+        max_slice_nums: int | None,
+    ) -> str | None:
+        """Placeholder text for one image, measured from its ``target_sizes``.
+
+        ``MiniCPMOcrProcessor.replace_image_token`` counts
+        ``target_sizes.prod(-1) // token_divisor`` per patch, row 0 being the
+        source image and row 1 a slice. Doing the same here keeps the count
+        correct for ``adaptive_small_image_upsize``, whose resize target is
+        decided from the pixels and cannot be recovered from ``image_size``.
+
+        ``target_sizes`` is already in *patch* units -- the image processor
+        stores ``source_h // patch_size`` -- so the divisor here is the bare
+        ``token_divisor``, unlike the pixel-side computation in
+        ``_compute_visual_tokens`` which also divides by ``patch_size ** 2``.
+
+        The slice grid is not pixel-dependent (``get_sliced_grid`` is a
+        function of the image size, ``max_slice_nums`` and
+        ``scale_resolution``), so it still comes from the geometry helper.
+        Returns ``None`` when the two disagree, leaving the caller on the 4.6
+        path rather than emitting a count we cannot justify.
+        """
+        info = self.info
+        assert isinstance(info, MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo)
+
+        if tgt_sizes.ndim != 2 or tgt_sizes.shape[-1] != 2 or tgt_sizes.shape[0] < 1:
+            return None
+
+        image_processor = info._pinned_image_processor(downsample_mode)
+        token_divisor = 4 if image_processor.downsample_mode == "4x" else 16
+
+        grids, _, _ = info._compute_visual_tokens(
+            image_size,
+            max_slice_nums,
+            downsample_mode=downsample_mode,
+        )
+        num_rows, num_cols = grids[0], grids[1]
+        if num_rows * num_cols + 1 != tgt_sizes.shape[0]:
+            return None
+
+        patch_tokens_per_slice = (
+            tgt_sizes.to(torch.long).prod(-1) // token_divisor
+        ).tolist()
+        source_tokens = int(patch_tokens_per_slice[0])
+        if source_tokens <= 0:

+        placeholder = (

+        if num_rows > 0 and num_cols > 0:
+            # `adaptive_tile_upsize` classifies each tile on its own crop, so
+            # slices in one grid can differ; emit one placeholder per tile.

+                slice_tokens = tile_tokens[0] if tile_tokens else 0
+                if slice_tokens > 0:
+                    slice_ph = slice_start + image_token * slice_tokens + slice_end
+                    rows = [slice_ph * num_cols for _ in range(num_rows)]
+                    placeholder += "\n".join(rows)
+            else:
+                if len(tile_tokens) != num_rows * num_cols:
+                    return None

+        image_embed_text = getattr(tokenizer, "image_token", "<|image_pad|>")
+        image_embed_ids = [tokenizer.get_vocab()[image_embed_text]]
+        image_items = out_mm_kwargs.get("image")
+

+            tgt_sizes = None
+            if image_items is not None and item_idx < len(image_items):
+                tgt_elem = image_items[item_idx].get("tgt_sizes")
+                if tgt_elem is not None and isinstance(tgt_elem.data, torch.Tensor):
+                    tgt_sizes = tgt_elem.data
+
+            if tgt_sizes is None:
+                # Image embeddings bypass the image processor, so there is no
+                # `target_sizes` to measure and no pixel-dependent resize.

+class CPUFp8ChannelWiseScaledMMLinearKernel(CPUFp8PerTensorScaledMMLinearKernel):
+    """FP8 W8A16 per-channel-scaled GEMM via AMX BRGEMM on CPU.
+
+    fp8_scaled_mm_cpu only supports block scales whose N extent is a multiple
+    of 32, so the GEMM runs with unit block scales and the per-output-channel
+    weight scale is applied to the output afterwards. Activations stay
+    BF16, regardless of the checkpoint's activation scheme.
+    """
+
+    @classmethod
+    def can_implement(cls, c: FP8ScaledMMLinearLayerConfig) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+        if not c.weight_quant_key.scale.group_shape.is_per_channel():
+            return False, "requires a per-channel weight scale."
+        if c.out_dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            return False, "Only bfloat16 output dtype supported."
+        n = c.weight_shape[0]
+        if n % 32 != 0:
+            return False, f"requires weight output dim (N={n}) to be a multiple of 32."
+        return True, None
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        w_name, w_s_name, _, _ = self.layer_param_names
+        weight = getattr(layer, w_name).t().contiguous()
+        n, k = weight.shape
+
+        packed_weight = torch.ops._C.convert_weight_packed(weight)
+        replace_parameter(
+            layer, w_name, torch.nn.Parameter(packed_weight, requires_grad=False)
+        )
+
+        self._block_size_n = n
+        num_k_blocks = -(-k // _BLOCK_SIZE_K)
+        self._unit_block_scale = torch.ones(1, num_k_blocks, dtype=torch.float32)
+        channel_scale = getattr(layer, w_s_name).reshape(-1).to(torch.float32)
+        replace_parameter(
+            layer, w_s_name, torch.nn.Parameter(channel_scale, requires_grad=False)
+        )
+
+    def apply_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        w_name, w_s_name, _, _ = self.layer_param_names
+        x_2d = x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1]) if x.dim() > 2 else x
+        out = torch.ops._C.fp8_scaled_mm_cpu(
+            x_2d,
+            getattr(layer, w_name),
+            self._unit_block_scale,
+            [self._block_size_n, _BLOCK_SIZE_K],
+            None,
+            x.dtype,
+            True,  # is_vnni (weight already prepacked)
+        )
+        out = (out.float() * getattr(layer, w_s_name)).to(x.dtype)
+        if bias is not None:
+            out += bias
+        return out.reshape(x.shape[:-1] + (out.size(-1),)) if x.dim() > 2 else out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Triton port of the fused GDN MTP decode kernel (``fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp``).
+
+The CUDA kernel in csrc only builds for CUDA 13, so on ROCm every Qwen3.5 GDN layer's
+speculative-decode step runs the unfused path: ~8 small copy/cat/fill kernels around the
+recurrent kernel plus the gated RMSNorm. This does the post-conv work in two launches.
+The update kernel reads q/k/v and a/b in place from the projections and runs the gated
+delta-rule update over each request's tokens (same state reads and writes as
+``fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update``: start from the state of the last accepted token,
+store the state after every token, slot index <= 0 means no state). Like that kernel it tiles
+the value dimension, so a small batch still fills the GPU; every tile writes its outputs and
+their sum of squares. The epilogue then applies the gated RMSNorm, the only step that needs
+the whole value dimension, and writes the out_proj input.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import num_compute_units
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gdn_mtp_update_kernel(
+    mixed_qkv,
+    b,
+    a,
+    A_log,
+    dt_bias,
+    state,
+    state_indices,
+    cu_seqlens,
+    num_accepted_tokens,
+    out,
+    sum_sq,
+    stride_qkv_row,
+    stride_b_row,
+    stride_a_row,
+    stride_state_slot,
+    stride_indices_row,
+    num_indices_per_row,
+    scale,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    HV: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    V: tl.constexpr,
+    BV: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    i_v, i_n, i_hv = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    NV: tl.constexpr = V // BV
+    i_h = i_hv // (HV // H)
+    bos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    num_tokens = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n + 1).to(tl.int64) - bos
+    if num_tokens <= 0:
+        return
+
+    o_k = tl.arange(0, K)
+    o_v = i_v * BV + tl.arange(0, BV)
+    p_out = out + (bos * HV + i_hv) * V + o_v
+    p_sum_sq = sum_sq + (bos * HV + i_hv) * NV + i_v
+    accepted = tl.load(num_accepted_tokens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    p_src = state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_row + accepted - 1
+    has_src = (accepted > 0) & (accepted <= num_indices_per_row)
+    src = tl.load(p_src, mask=has_src, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    if src <= 0:
+        for t in range(num_tokens):
+            tl.store(p_out + t * HV * V, tl.zeros([BV], dtype=out.dtype.element_ty))
+            tl.store(p_sum_sq + t * HV * NV, 0.0)
+        return
+
+    p_state = i_hv * V * K + o_v[:, None] * K + o_k[None, :]
+    b_h = tl.load(state + src * stride_state_slot + p_state).to(tl.float32)
+    neg_A = -tl.exp(tl.load(A_log + i_hv).to(tl.float32))
+    bias = tl.load(dt_bias + i_hv).to(tl.float32)
+    for t in range(num_tokens):
+        row = bos + t
+        p_qkv = mixed_qkv + row * stride_qkv_row
+        b_q = tl.load(p_qkv + i_h * K + o_k).to(tl.float32)
+        b_k = tl.load(p_qkv + (H + i_h) * K + o_k).to(tl.float32)
+        b_v = tl.load(p_qkv + 2 * H * K + i_hv * V + o_v).to(tl.float32)
+        x = tl.load(a + row * stride_a_row + i_hv).to(tl.float32) + bias
+        decay = tl.exp(neg_A * tl.where(x <= 20.0, tl.log(1 + tl.exp(x)), x))
+        beta = tl.sigmoid(tl.load(b + row * stride_b_row + i_hv).to(tl.float32))
+
+        b_q = b_q * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(b_q * b_q) + 1e-6) * scale
+        b_k = b_k * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(b_k * b_k) + 1e-6)
+        b_h *= decay
+        b_v = (b_v - tl.sum(b_h * b_k[None, :], 1)) * beta
+        b_h += b_v[:, None] * b_k[None, :]
+        # Rounded like the unfused path, whose recurrent kernel stores it first.
+        b_o = tl.sum(b_h * b_q[None, :], 1).to(out.dtype.element_ty)
+        tl.store(p_out + t * HV * V, b_o)
+        b_o = b_o.to(tl.float32)
+        tl.store(p_sum_sq + t * HV * NV, tl.sum(b_o * b_o))
+
+        dst = tl.load(state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_row + t).to(tl.int64)
+        if dst > 0:
+            p_dst = state + dst * stride_state_slot + p_state
+            tl.store(p_dst, b_h.to(state.dtype.element_ty))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gdn_mtp_gated_rmsnorm_kernel(
+    out,
+    sum_sq,
+    z,
+    norm_weight,
+    cu_seqlens,
+    stride_z_row,
+    eps,
+    HV: tl.constexpr,
+    V: tl.constexpr,
+    NV: tl.constexpr,
+    SIGMOID_GATE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    i_n, i_hv, t = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    bos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    if t >= tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n + 1).to(tl.int64) - bos:
+        return
+
+    row = bos + t
+    o_v = tl.arange(0, V)
+    p_out = out + (row * HV + i_hv) * V + o_v
+    b_o = tl.load(p_out).to(tl.float32)
+    p_sum_sq = sum_sq + (row * HV + i_hv) * NV + tl.arange(0, NV)
+    rstd = tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(tl.load(p_sum_sq)) / V + eps)
+    b_z = tl.load(z + row * stride_z_row + i_hv * V + o_v).to(tl.float32)
+    if SIGMOID_GATE:
+        gate = tl.sigmoid(b_z)
+    else:
+        gate = b_z * tl.sigmoid(b_z)
+    w = tl.load(norm_weight + o_v).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(p_out, (b_o * rstd * w * gate).to(out.dtype.element_ty))
+
+
+def fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp_triton(
+    mixed_qkv: torch.Tensor,
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+    num_accepted_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+    state: torch.Tensor,
+    output_gate: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    norm_eps: float,
+    output_gate_activation: str,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Same arguments and result as ``ops.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp``.
+

+    assert dt_bias.is_contiguous() and dt_bias.numel() == HV
+    assert state.dim() == 4 and state.shape[1:3] == (HV, V)
+    assert state.stride(1) == V * K and state.stride(2) == K and state.stride(3) == 1

+    assert num_accepted_tokens.is_contiguous()
+    assert num_accepted_tokens.numel() == num_requests
+    assert output_gate.shape == out.shape == (num_tokens, HV, V)
+    assert output_gate.stride(2) == 1 and output_gate.stride(1) == V
+    assert out.is_contiguous()
+    assert norm_weight.is_contiguous() and norm_weight.numel() == V
+    assert output_gate_activation in ("silu", "sigmoid")
+    # Tile V only while the GPU needs more programs: 32 rows per program while there are fewer

+    sum_sq = torch.empty(
+        (out.shape[0], HV, V // BV), dtype=torch.float32, device=out.device
+    )
+    _gdn_mtp_update_kernel[(V // BV, num_requests, HV)](

+        b,
+        a,
+        A_log,
+        dt_bias,
+        state,
+        state_indices,
+        cu_seqlens,
+        num_accepted_tokens,
+        out,
+        sum_sq,
+        mixed_qkv.stride(0),
+        b.stride(0),
+        a.stride(0),
+        state.stride(0),
+        state_indices.stride(0),
+        state_indices.shape[1],
+        scale,
+        H=H,
+        HV=HV,
+        K=K,
+        V=V,
+        BV=BV,
+        num_warps=4,

+        norm_weight,

+        V=V,
+        NV=V // BV,
+        SIGMOID_GATE=output_gate_activation == "sigmoid",
+        num_warps=2,

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiniMax-M3 rejects IndexCache keys passed as top-level --hf-overrides."""
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.config import ModelConfig
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model import _should_skip_index_topk
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.transformers_utils.configs.minimax_m3 import MiniMaxM3Config
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="MiniMax-M3 AMD model"
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def checkpoint(tmp_path_factory):
+    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("minimax_m3")
+    MiniMaxM3Config(
+        architectures=["MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration"]
+    ).save_pretrained(path)
+    return str(path)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("hf_overrides", "expected_error"),
+    [
+        (
+            {
+                "use_index_cache": True,
+                "index_topk_freq": 2,
+                "index_skip_topk_offset": 1,
+            },
+            (
+                "top-level use_index_cache, index_topk_freq, index_skip_topk_offset "
+                'would be ignored. Pass them as --hf-overrides \'{"text_config": '
+                '{"use_index_cache": true, "index_topk_freq": 2, '
+                '"index_skip_topk_offset": 1}}\'.'
+            ),
+        ),
+        (
+            {"use_index_cache": True, "text_config": {"index_topk_freq": 2}},
+            (
+                "top-level use_index_cache would be ignored. Pass them as "
+                '--hf-overrides \'{"text_config": {"use_index_cache": true}}\'.'
+            ),
+        ),
+    ],
+    ids=["top_level", "mixed"],
+)
+def test_top_level_overrides_are_rejected(checkpoint, hf_overrides, expected_error):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=re.escape(expected_error)):
+        ModelConfig(checkpoint, hf_overrides=hf_overrides)
+

@@ -0,0 +1,351 @@
+meta:
+  title: "MiniMax-M3.1-Flash"
+  slug: "minimax-m3.1-flash"
+  provider: "MiniMax"
+  description: "MiniMax M3.1-Flash vision-language MoE (~428B total / 23B active) with MSA sparse attention throughout and a built-in DSpark draft; quantization-aware trained, MXFP8 dense layers and NVFP4 experts. Served TP4 on NVIDIA GB200 or AMD MI355X, single node or prefill/decode disaggregated."
+  date_added: 2026-10-23
+  date_updated: 2026-10-23
+  tasks:
+    - text
+    - multimodal
+  performance_headline: "MSA sparse attention, 1M context, DSpark speculative decoding built into the checkpoint"
+  related_recipes: ["MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3"]
+  default_hardware: b300
+  hardware:
+    mi355x: verified
+    b300: verified
+    gb200: verified
+    gb300: verified
+
+model:
+  model_id: "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash"
+  min_vllm_version: "0.33.0"
+  nightly_required: true
+  docker_image:
+    nvidia: "vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash"
+    amd: "vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash"
+  architecture: moe
+  # From the model card (~428B total, 23B activated per token); the
+  # safetensors headers count 427.05B (experts 413.1B, vision 0.9B).
+  parameter_count: "428B"
+  active_parameters: "23B"
+  context_length: 1048576
+  base_args:
+    # MSA's sparse_block_size is 128 — KV cache block size must match.
+    - "--block-size"
+    - "128"
+    - "--kv-cache-dtype"
+    - "nvfp4"
+    - "--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager"
+  base_env: {}
+
+features:
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "MiniMax M3 tool call parser with automatic tool choice"
+    args:
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "minimax_m3"
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+  reasoning:
+    description: "MiniMax M3 reasoning parser"
+    args:
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "minimax_m3"
+  spec_decoding:
+    description: "DSpark speculative decoding with the draft shipped in the checkpoint (`dspark/`), three speculative tokens, FP8 draft KV cache. Draft attention backend is per-brand: FLASH_ATTN on NVIDIA, TRITON_ATTN on AMD."
+    # Per-brand draft attention backend (a feature's top-level `args` is the
+    # fallback when no hardware_overrides.<gen> matches; both brands are
+    # covered here).
+    hardware_overrides:
+      nvidia:
+        args:
+          - "--speculative-config"
+          - '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}'
+      amd:
+        args:
+          - "--speculative-config"
+          - '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
+  text_only:
+    description: "Skip loading the vision encoder for text-only workloads — frees VRAM for KV cache."
+    args:
+      - "--language-model-only"
+
+opt_in_features:
+  - text_only
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    # One checkpoint for both brands: MXFP8 dense layers + NVFP4 experts. The
+    # empty precision_hardware lifts the NVFP4 => NVIDIA Blackwell default;
+    # supported_hardware lists the eligible GPUs (meta.hardware marks the
+    # verified ones).
+    precision: nvfp4
+    precision_hardware: {}
+    supported_hardware:
+      - mi355x
+      - gb200
+      - gb300
+      - b200
+      - b300
+    # MI355X re-quantizes the experts to MXFP8 at load: 413.1B x 1.03 bytes +
+    # 17.5 GB of other weights ≈ 444 GB, x 1.2 ≈ 533 GB.
+    vram_minimum_gb: 533
+    description: "MXFP8 dense layers + NVFP4 experts with NVFP4 KV and indexer K caches. GB200 runs the NVFP4 experts natively; MI355X re-quantizes them to MXFP8 for the AITER MoE."
+    hardware_overrides:
+      # GB200 runs the NVFP4 experts natively: 413.1B x 0.53 bytes + 17.5 GB
+      # ≈ 237 GB, x 1.2 ≈ 285 GB.
+      gb200:
+        vram_minimum_gb: 285
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  single_node_tp:
+    # One GB200 tray, or half of an 8-GPU MI355X node.
+    tp: 4
+
+hardware_overrides:
+  nvidia:
+    extra_args:
+      - "--attention-config"
+      - '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}'
+      - "--compilation-config"
+      - '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'
+    extra_env:
+      VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION: "high"
+  amd:
+    extra_args:
+      - "--attention-config"
+      - '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "indexer_decode_cp": true}'
+      - "--quantization-config.moe"
+      - "mxfp8"
+    extra_env:
+      VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER: "1"
+      VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS: "1"
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [MiniMax-M3.1-Flash](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) is a
+  vision-language MoE model from [MiniMax](https://www.minimax.io/) that keeps
+  the MoE architecture of [MiniMax-M3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3):
+  about 428B total / 23B active parameters and a 1M-token context, with MSA
+  sparse attention in every layer.
+
+  - **Quantization-aware training** — the checkpoint stores MXFP8 dense layers
+    and NVFP4 experts.
+  - **Built-in DSpark draft** — the `dspark/` directory of the checkpoint;
+    `--speculative-config` needs no draft model path.
+  - **Native multimodal** — image and video inputs.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **AMD:** MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2+, TP4.
+  - **NVIDIA:** GB200 (Blackwell), TP4 on half a node; NVFP4 MoE runs natively
+    on the FP4 tensor cores.
+  - **`--block-size 128` is mandatory** (MSA sparse/index cache).
+
+  ## Launching the Server
+
+  ### Single node (TP4, AMD MI355X)
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
+  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    -tp 4 \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "indexer_decode_cp": true}' \
+    --quantization-config.moe mxfp8 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
+    --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
+  ```
+
+  - `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` and `indexer_kv_dtype: nvfp4` store the KV cache
+    and the sparse-attention indexer's K cache in NVFP4.
+  - `indexer_decode_cp` splits the indexer's decode scoring across the TP ranks
+    by context instead of by index head.
+  - `--quantization-config.moe mxfp8` re-quantizes the NVFP4 experts to MXFP8 at
+    load for the AITER MoE.
+
+  ### Single node (TP4, NVIDIA GB200)
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high \
+  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    -tp 4 \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}' \
+    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
+    --max-num-seqs 256 \
+    --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
+  ```
+
+  - Blackwell runs the NVFP4 experts natively, so no
+    `--quantization-config.moe` override is needed.
+  - `use_prefill_query_quantization` quantizes the prefill query on the MSA
+    indexer path (Q8KV4).
+
+  ### Prefill/decode disaggregation (1P1D, TP4 + TP4, AMD MI355X)
+
+  Prefill node:
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
+  VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=<P_IP> \
+  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    -tp 4 \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4"}' \
+    --quantization-config.moe mxfp8 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
+    --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
+    --port 8100 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
+      {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"num_threads":4}},
+      {"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":601295421440,"cpu_hugepage_block_size":"1GB","lazy_offload":false}}]}}'
+  ```
+
+  Decode node:
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
+  VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=<D_IP> \
+  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    -tp 4 \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "indexer_decode_cp": true}' \
+    --quantization-config.moe mxfp8 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
+    --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
+    --port 8200 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"num_threads":4}}'
+  ```
+
+  - `<P_IP>` and `<D_IP>` are each node's own address, reachable from the
+    other node (the NIXL side channel).
+  - `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC` goes on both nodes. It keeps all layers of a
+    block contiguous, so NIXL reads one region per block instead of one per
+    layer.
+  - The prefill node never decodes, so it leaves `indexer_decode_cp` off.
+  - The prefill node also offloads KV to host memory
+    (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`): 560 GiB per rank in 1 GiB HugeTLB pages, so
+    2240 pages for the four ranks. Reserve them on the host before the start
+    (and allow them in the container's hugetlb limit), or the server fails at
+    startup with `Cannot map 560.00 GiB of 1024 MiB HugeTLB pages`:
+
+    ```bash
+    echo 2240 | sudo tee /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-1048576kB/nr_hugepages
+    ```
+
+  ### Prefill/decode disaggregation (1P1D, TP4 + TP4, NVIDIA GB200)
+
+  The NVIDIA pair runs NVFP4 KV end to end over NIXL (kv_buffer_device
+  `cuda`); the prefill node skips CUDA graphs (`--enforce-eager`) and carries
+  a 32768-token batch budget, the decode node runs FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs.
+
+  Prefill node:
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=<P_IP> \
+  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    -tp 4 \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4"}' \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
+    --max-num-seqs 16 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+    --enforce-eager \
+    --port 8100 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"enforce_handshake_compat":false,"kv_lease_duration":120}}'
+  ```
+
+  Decode node:
+
+  ```bash
+  VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=<D_IP> \
+  vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    -tp 4 \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
+    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}' \
+    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
+    --max-num-seqs 88 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+    --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
+    --port 8200 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"enforce_handshake_compat":false,"kv_lease_duration":120}}'
+  ```
+
+  For a quick test, put the toy NIXL proxy from the vLLM repository in front of
+  the two nodes and send requests to port 8000:
+
+  ```bash
+  python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py --port 8000 \
+    --prefiller-host <P_IP> --prefiller-port 8100 \
+    --decoder-host <D_IP> --decoder-port 8200
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  Recommended sampling parameters (from the model card): `temperature = 1.0`,
+  `top_p = 0.95`. Set the reasoning effort per request with
+  `chat_template_kwargs: {"reasoning_effort": "<level>"}`: `low`, `medium`,
+  `high`, `xhigh` or `max`.
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+      "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash",
+      "temperature": 1.0,
+      "top_p": 0.95,
+      "messages": [
+        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain MSA sparse attention in 3 bullets."}
+      ]
+    }'
+  ```
+
+  ## Benchmarking
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm bench serve \
+    --backend vllm \
+    --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
+    --endpoint /v1/completions \
+    --dataset-name random \
+    --random-input 8192 \
+    --random-output 1024 \
+    --max-concurrency 32 \
+    --num-prompts 320
+  ```
+
+  ## Troubleshooting
+
+  - **`--block-size` mismatch.** MSA's sparse block size is 128; the vLLM KV
+    cache block size must match (otherwise `No common block size for 16`).
+  - **Parsers.** `--tool-call-parser` and `--reasoning-parser` both use
+    `minimax_m3`.
+  - **HugeTLB pages (PD prefill node).** See the PD section above.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash)
+  - [MiniMax-M3 recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3)
+  - [MiniMax](https://www.minimax.io/)

@@ -82,6 +82,29 @@ cache), see [ECMooncakeConnector Usage Guide](mooncake_ec_connector_usage.md).
 - **device_name**: Comma-separated whitelist of RDMA devices (e.g. `"mlx5_0,mlx5_1"`) to restrict topology discovery to. Empty discovers every device. Useful on hosts exposing a mix of InfiniBand and RoCE ports, where both peers must settle on the same link layer.
 - **bootstrap_server_address**: Optional `"host:port"` of an already running Mooncake bootstrap server. All prefiller ranks register with this endpoint instead of launching an embedded server. The caller owns the server lifetime and must configure the proxy to use the same endpoint. The example proxy assumes the bootstrap server is on the prefiller API host; a different host requires a proxy that supplies that address in `remote_bootstrap_addr`. Omit this option to use the embedded server and `VLLM_MOONCAKE_BOOTSTRAP_PORT`.
 
+## Prometheus metrics
+
+The following Prometheus metrics are exported when MooncakeConnector is active, each with the standard `model_name` and `engine` labels:
+
+| Metric name | Type | Description |
+| ------------- | ------ | ------------- |
+| `vllm:mooncake_xfer_time_seconds` | Histogram | Per-transfer copy duration (seconds). |
+| `vllm:mooncake_bytes_transferred` | Histogram | Bytes moved per transfer. |
+| `vllm:mooncake_num_descriptors` | Histogram | Descriptor count per transfer. |
+| `vllm:mooncake_num_failed_transfers` | Counter | Cumulative count of failed KV-block transfers. |
+| `vllm:mooncake_num_failed_recvs` | Counter | Cumulative count of failed KV-block receives. |
+| `vllm:mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs` | Counter | Requests whose KV blocks expired on the prefiller before the decoder read them (tracked on the P instance). |
+
+!!! note
+    Mooncake is push-based: the prefiller (P) performs the transfer, so the
+    three histograms are only populated on P instances, while the decoder (D)
+    reports only the failures it observes.
+
+!!! tip
+    High `vllm:mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs` indicates that the prefiller's
+    lease duration is too short for your network or workload. Increase it via
+    `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`.
+

 Refer to these example scripts in the vLLM repository:

+    def __init__(

+        labelnames: list[str],

+            name="vllm:mooncake_num_failed_transfers",
+            documentation="Number of failed Mooncake KV Cache transfers.",
+            labelnames=labelnames,
+        )
+        self.counter_mooncake_num_failed_transfers = create_metric_per_engine(
+            counter_mooncake_num_failed_transfers, self.per_engine_labelvalues
+        )
+        counter_mooncake_num_failed_recvs = self._counter_cls(
+            name="vllm:mooncake_num_failed_recvs",
+            documentation="Number of failed Mooncake KV Cache receives.",
+            labelnames=labelnames,
+        )
+        self.counter_mooncake_num_failed_recvs = create_metric_per_engine(
+            counter_mooncake_num_failed_recvs, self.per_engine_labelvalues
+        )
+        counter_mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs = self._counter_cls(
+            name="vllm:mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs",
+            documentation="Number of requests that had their KV expire. "
+            "NOTE: This metric is tracked on the P instance.",
+            labelnames=labelnames,
+        )
+        self.counter_mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs = create_metric_per_engine(
+            counter_mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs, self.per_engine_labelvalues
+        )

+    def observe(self, transfer_stats_data: dict[str, Any], engine_idx: int = 0) -> None:
+        # A snapshot always carries every declared key, so a miss here is a
+        # connector bug and should surface rather than silently drop samples.
+        for per_engine_metrics, stats_key in (
+            (self.mooncake_histogram_xfer_time, "transfer_duration"),
+            (self.mooncake_histogram_bytes_transferred, "bytes_transferred"),
+            (self.mooncake_histogram_num_descriptors, "num_descriptors"),

+        # one Prometheus client call per series instead of one per event.
+        for per_engine_metrics, stats_key in (
+            (self.counter_mooncake_num_failed_transfers, "num_failed_transfers"),
+            (self.counter_mooncake_num_failed_recvs, "num_failed_recvs"),
+            (self.counter_mooncake_num_kv_expired_reqs, "num_kv_expired_reqs"),
+        ):
+            num_events = sum(transfer_stats_data[stats_key])
+            if num_events:
+                per_engine_metrics[engine_idx].inc(num_events)

+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_f16_auto.cu"
+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_bf16_auto.cu"
+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_bf16_auto.cu"
+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_f16_fp8_f16.cu"
+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_f16_fp8_f16.cu"

+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_bf16_fp8_fp8.cu"
+    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_bf16_fp8_fp8.cu")
+
+  # Each attention_paged_attn_*.cu file below instantiates one kernel set and
+  # exposes it as one entry point. That entry point is only reachable if
+  # paged_attention() in csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu names it in one of its
+  # ATTN_HEAD_SWITCH() calls (the dispatch arms); otherwise the file is compiled
+  # and linked unnecessarily. Fail at configure time instead.
+  file(READ "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu" _attn_dispatch)
+  string(FIND "${_attn_dispatch}" "#define ATTN_HEAD_SWITCH" _attn_arms_pos)

+    message(FATAL_ERROR

+      "update the instantiation guard in CMakeLists.txt accordingly.")
+  endif()
+  string(SUBSTRING "${_attn_dispatch}" ${_attn_arms_pos} -1 _attn_arms)
+  foreach (_attn_src ${VLLM_ROCM_EXT_SRC})
+    if (_attn_src MATCHES "^csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_.*\\.cu$")
+      file(READ "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/${_attn_src}" _attn_tu)
+      string(REGEX MATCHALL "ATTN_ENTRY\\([A-Za-z0-9_]+\\)" _attn_entries
+        "${_attn_tu}")
+      foreach (_attn_entry ${_attn_entries})
+        string(REGEX REPLACE "ATTN_ENTRY\\((.*)\\)" "\\1" _attn_name

+            "csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu never dispatches it: the file "

@@ -169,6 +169,24 @@ llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-8B", enable_sleep_mode=True, enable_nccl_comm_suspend=True
 
 or `vllm serve <model> --enable-sleep-mode --enable-nccl-comm-suspend`.
 
+#### Choosing a sleep-mode backend
+
+`sleep_mode_backend` selects how GPU memory is freed and restored. The default
+is the built-in `cumem` backend. Plugins can register other backends with
+`SleepModeBackendFactory.register_backend` from a `vllm.general_plugins` entry
+point, and you select one by name:
+
+```python
+llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-8B", enable_sleep_mode=True, sleep_mode_backend="my_backend")
+```
+
+or `vllm serve <model> --enable-sleep-mode --sleep-mode-backend my_backend`.
+
+An unregistered name is not caught at startup; it fails the first time the
+backend is used, such as on the first sleep. CUDA graph offloading and
+`release_kv_cache_memory()` have their own backend requirements, described
+above.
+
 ### Online Serving
 
 To enable sleep mode in a vLLM server you need to initialize it with the flag `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` and pass `--enable-sleep-mode` to the vLLM server.

+        OpenMP env setup on the CPU backend and the NUMA numactl wrapper both

+            and self.local_world_size > 1
+            and not current_platform.is_cpu()
+            and not self.parallel_config.numa_bind
+        )

+    def _start_workers_concurrently(

+        unready_workers: list["UnreadyWorkerProcHandle"],
